deep.reconstruction:
Setting (continued from the previous pages). π = π̂ is the profinite fundamental group of P^1 − {0,1,∞}. It is generated by inertia generators l_0, l_1, l_∞ with l_0 l_1 l_∞ = 1, so it is free profinite on l_0, l_1. L_i denotes the procyclic subgroup topologically generated by l_i. G_3 ≅ S_3 acts by outer automorphisms, permuting the three punctures. ρ is the 3-cycle (l_0 ↦ l_1 ↦ l_∞), generating C_3. σ_∞ is the transposition 0↔1, with l_0 ↔ l_1. Grothendieck studies outer automorphisms u of π that normalize L_0, with u(l_0) = l_0^p (p ∈ Ẑ^*), and that commute with ρ up to inner, uρ = int(g)ρu. The previous page showed such u is determined by (p,g): u(l_1) = int(g)l_1^p and u(l_∞) = int(gρ(g))l_∞^p. It also gave the condition that u respects l_0 l_1 l_∞ = 1, namely int(g^{-1})l_0^p · l_1^p · int(ρ(g))l_∞^p = 1, which is the precursor of Drinfeld's 3-cycle relation.

This page:
(i) Grothendieck asks how to see that (p,g) gives an automorphism and not just an endomorphism, and finds this 'délicat'.
(ii) Test case τ (complex conjugation): p = −1, g = l_1, and τρ = int(l_1)ρτ.
(iii) He now requires u to commute (as an outer automorphism) with all of G_3, not only C_3. It suffices to add σ_∞: there should exist h ∈ π, unique given u, with uσ_∞ = int(h)σ_∞u. It suffices to test this on l_0 and l_1.
- On l_0: int(g)l_1^p = int(h)l_1^p. Since the centralizer of l_1^p in the free profinite group is L_1, this gives g^{-1}h ∈ L_1, i.e. h = g l_1^q with q ∈ Ẑ.
- On l_1: l_0^p = int(hσ_∞(g))l_0^p, hence g l_1^q σ_∞(g) ∈ L_0.
So the S_3-compatibility condition is: there exists q with g l_1^q σ_∞(g) ∈ L_0. On the next page this becomes g l_1^q σ_∞(g) = l_0^r. He checks that (q,r) is invariant under the normalization g ↦ l_0^α g l_1^{−α}, and that for τ one gets q = −1, r = 1. A margin remark there renormalizes to σ_∞(g') = l_0^β g l_1^β. With Drinfeld's normalization this is exactly the 2-cycle relation f(x,y)f(y,x) = 1.
The overall problem is to describe the image of Gal(Q̄/Q), or a combinatorial envelope of it, inside Out(π̂_{0,3}) via S_3-equivariance. These are the defining equations of what became the Grothendieck–Teichmüller group GT̂ (Drinfeld 1990; Ihara).
errors: No mathematical errors. The step g^{-1}h ∈ L_1 uses, without saying so, that the centralizer of l_1^p (p a unit) in the free profinite group is L_1. This is true, but not justified on the page.

The endomorphism vs. automorphism question is left open. The modern resolution: a finitely generated profinite group is Hopfian, so a surjective continuous endomorphism is an automorphism. Surjectivity still has to be checked; Drinfeld simply defines GT̂ as the invertible elements of the monoid of solutions.

ideas.what: Parametrizing L_0-normalizing outer automorphisms of π̂_{0,3} commuting with C_3 by pairs (p,g) ∈ Ẑ^* × π̂, with u(l_0) = l_0^p and u(l_1) = g l_1^p g^{-1}
ideas.modern_name: Elements (λ,f) of the Grothendieck–Teichmüller monoid/group GT̂, with g ↔ f^{-1}
ideas.where_published: The Teichmüller-tower programme is in Esquisse d'un programme (1984) and La Longue Marche (1981), but without these explicit equations as far as I know

ideas.what: Condition for compatibility with σ_∞: there exist q, r with g l_1^q σ_∞(g) = l_0^r, invariant under g ↦ l_0^α g l_1^{−α}
ideas.modern_name: 2-cycle relation f(x,y)f(y,x) = 1 in the definition of GT̂

ideas.what: Complex conjugation as the test case τ: p = −1, g = l_1, (q,r) = (−1,1)
Question whether an endomorphism defined by (p,g) is automatically an automorphism
ideas.modern_name: Invertibility in the GT monoid; Hopfian property of f.g. profinite groups
ideas.usually_credited_to: Drinfeld (monoid vs. group); standard profinite group theory

missed.claim: In spring 1981 Grothendieck derives, in explicit equations, the S_3-equivariance conditions on (p,g) for outer automorphisms of π̂_{0,3}. These are the 3-cycle relation (previous page) and the 2-cycle relation (this page). Together they are essentially the genus-0, 3-point part of the definition of GT̂, nine years before Drinfeld.
missed.quote: ∃q tel que g l_1^q σ_∞(g) ∈ L_0
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This documents precisely that Grothendieck had the GT̂ defining relations (without the pentagon) in 1981. The literature usually credits the explicit equations to Drinfeld/Ihara, with Grothendieck credited only for the programmatic idea.

missed.claim: He explicitly flags as delicate whether solutions (p,g) give automorphisms rather than endomorphisms, and leaves it unresolved here.
missed.quote: Mais comment vérifier que (p;g) définissent non seulement un endomorphisme, mais un automorphisme ? Ça semble délicat...
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is the same issue Drinfeld sidestepped by passing to invertible elements of the monoid. It is of minor historical interest only.

deep.surprise_reason: The page contains an explicit 1981 derivation of the 2-cycle relation of GT̂, in the form g l_1^q σ_∞(g) ∈ L_0, together with its normalization. It is known that Grothendieck envisaged the S_3/Teichmüller-tower approach in La Longue Marche and the Esquisse. But the explicit equations are generally attributed to Drinfeld 1990, so this is a notable precursor detail, though not a new result.
transcription_corrections: Line 1: '(ρ;g)' should be '(p;g)'. The image shows p, the exponent, not ρ.

The insertion above 'la commutation de u' is very uncertain. It looks like something about the 'structure ... tacite/discrète' and should be marked illegible rather than read as 'respectant la structure discrète'.
'(C_3)^+' is likely just 'C_3' followed by a comma; the '+' is doubtful.

The derivation lines are reorganized in the transcription. The image has u σ_∞(l_0) = int(h) σ_∞(l_0^p), with underbraces u(l_1) = int(g)l_1^p and σ_∞(l_0^p) = l_1^p, then 'i.e. int(g^{-1}h) l_1^p = l_1^p i.e. g^{-1}h ∈ L_1 i.e. h = g l_1^q, q ∈ Ẑ'.
The second condition in the image is u σ_∞(l_1) = int(h) σ_∞ u(l_1), with underbraces σ_∞(l_1) = l_0 and u(l_1) = int(g) l_1^p.
The left margin note is largely illegible. It seems to begin 'NB Ici il importe...' and to concern extending the automorphism of π to an outer automorphism respecting the extra structure.
